Many appreciated the official mod support and rushed to download mods.

On October 22, CD Projekt RED returned to Cyberpunk 2077 and released a major update 2.5. The game added content in the style of the anime "Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2," new features, various improvements, and official mod support on consoles via the mod.io platform — similar to the recent The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt remaster.

Soon, mod.io representatives recorded a record number of mod downloads. It turned out that within 24 hours, modifications for Cyberpunk 2077 were downloaded 2.8 million times.

Paweł Sasko, the quest director of the original game and game director of the sequel, reacted to this event — as usual, his message was accompanied by a crying (of joy) emoji:

items.title: ‘Cyberpunk 2077’ Rockets To Its Second-Highest Playercount Since Launch
Cyberpunk 2077 gets titan-sized crossover with dead EA FPS
items.content:
Cyberpunk 2077 has brought back a series long-since dead due to EA's stupidity.

Cyberpunk 2077 was already a peak gameplay experience, but it gets even better now that it’s somewhat revived a long-dead franchise.

Later this week, CD Projekt RED will return to Night City with a new update , centred around the newly released Cyberpunk: Edgerunners Season 2 .

While we don’t know what new content will be added, we’re excited nonetheless, though not as excited as we are for Cyberpunk 2 .

In the meantime, the best source of new Cyberpunk 2077 content, aside from CD Projekt Red itself, is NexusMods, and we’ve found a good one this week.

Titanfall BT-7274 (Quest and Companion) by whatmynickname and sdh0 is available on NexusMods right now, and it’s a must-play for fans of the Titanfall series.

As the name implies, it makes your Titanfall 2 companion BT-7274 an in-game NPC, and he’s a force to be reckoned with.

BT-7274 doesn’t join you right off the bat though. You’ll have to track him down through a new quest set in the Badlands.

Once you’ve found him, he can be summoned from the sky whenever you need some extra muscle. You can of course, pilot him yourself if you’d prefer.

It’s an impressive overhaul, but of course, like most of the mods we’ve been seeing nowadays, it comes with a catch. This has obviously been created with the help of AI tools. That’s not something we can get behind, unfortunately, so we won’t be using this mod ourselves, but for those who couldn’t care less, this looks like an explosive expansion worth trying for yourself.

READ NEXT: Cyberpunk 2077 players can now possess enemies in free mod, opening up a whole new play style

Seeing BT-7274 again got us thinking about the immense disappointment the Titanfall series turned out to be.

That initial first release was unlike anything we’d seen before and the follow-up was pure magic. Respawn found a great balance between a heartfelt single-player campaign and a consistently fun multiplayer; sequels were all but inevitable.

Unfortunately, for whatever reason, we’ve not heard a peep about new Titanfall games since. The series somewhat lives on through APEX Legends , but it’s nowhere near the same thing.

items.title: Hideo Kojima Reprises Cyberpunk 2077 Character in Edgerunners 2
items.summary: Kojima voices Hideyoshi Oshima in video game & anime
items.content:
(In)famous video game director Hideo Kojima confirmed on Monday that he performed in the new original net anime series Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 . The director said he is reprising his Cyberpunk 2077 character Hideyoshi Oshima, a braindance producer, in a cameo appearance in the new anime. Kojima also posted a handful of photos of his voice recording session: Image via x.com © 2026 CD PROJEKT RED S.A. CD PROJEKT RED, the CD PROJEKT RED logo, Cyberpunk, Cyberpunk 2077 and the Cyberpunk 2077 logo are trademarks and/or registered trademarks of CD PROJEKT RED S.A. in the US and/or other countries. Image via x.com ©小島秀夫

Kojima made a cameo appearance in CD PROJEKT RED 's 2020 cyberpunk video game Cyberpunk 2077 as Hideyoshi Oshima. The video game itself draws inspiration from the Cyberpunk tabletop role-playing game series created by Mike Pondsmith in 1988. The tabletop game has seen several editions, including Cyberpunk 2013 , Cyberpunk 2020 , Cyberpunk V3.0 , and the latest edition Cyberpunk Red .

Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 is the sequel to the first Cyberpunk: Edgerunners anime , which Studio Trigger produced based on CD PROJEKT RED 's Cyberpunk 2077 game. The first series premiered on Netflix in September 2022.

The Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 anime premiered on October 20 on Netflix .

items.title: Mass Effect 5 was "something special", dev says – it was BioWare's response to what Baldur's Gate 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 devs "were bringing to the table"
items.content:
It might've taken the RPG series "to the next level"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: BioWare) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 5 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Mass Effect 5 is no more following the closure of BioWare after the EA buyout – but former developers believe it would've been an incredible RPG, had it come to fruition.

Tony de Waal, who acted as cinematic supervisor at BioWare and boasted some 29 years of experience at the studio, implies as much in a new LinkedIn post, explaining that he worked on everything from Mass Effect 2 to Dragon Age: The Veilguard – a game he says "was a herculean effort that tested the limits of even my workaholic mindset" – before Mass Effect 5. "I believe we were making something special," he describes. "A level of autonomy and choice that no other game has been able to match." The dev then references Baldur's Gate 3 team Larian Studios and CD Projekt Red, masterminds behind The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 , recalling how BioWare looked to them: "We saw what Larian and CD Projekt were bringing to the table with their latest offerings, and started down a path to bring Mass Effect to the next level while remaining true to the Trilogy."

The cinematic mastermind closes by admitting "I'm sad you won't ever get to see what we were cooking" and paying tribute to his fellow devs, "some of the most talented people I've had the pleasure of working with throughout my career." Interestingly, though, de Waal isn't the only BioWare veteran to reference Mass Effect 5 and how good it might've played had it been given the chance it deserved from EA to actually come to life.

Over on X , Derek Künsken, who introduces himself as both "a contract writer, and as a senior writer on staff" from BioWare, echoes this sentiment. He isn't able to share too much aside from the fact that he was working on the new Mass Effect title and "what we were cooking was really cool," but that's got me wondering what could've been just as much as de Waal's own words do. I'm sure "really cool" is no understatement, after all.

It's disappointing to know that we won't get to experience what the devs had in store with Mass Effect 5 – and doubly so after hearing how amazing it may have been.

Mass Effect 5 would have been Mass Effect Universe, and one trailer has changed how I see the entire series Mass Effect 5: The new Mass Effect game has been canceled, here's everything we know The Witcher and Cyberpunk 2077 devs join creators mourning BioWare EA killing BioWare could lead to Mass Effect and Dragon Age rights being sold, former lead says, but they could just as easily "bury them in the vault"

items.title: From the Anime to the Game — Free Update Brings Edgerunners 2 Content and More to Cyberpunk 2077!
items.summary: The free Edgerunners 2 Update to Cyberpunk 2077 is available now, with content inspired by the second installment of the hit anime series now streaming on Netflix
items.content:
“Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2” premiered on Netflix on October 20, bringing a whole new cast of characters to Night City for a dark, gritty ride. And now we’re bringing a little piece of that story into Cyberpunk 2077 , too! The free Edgerunners 2 Update is here, with content inspired by the anime, new ways to fight, more customization options, and plenty of other additions.

We’ve got a lot to cover, so let’s get into it. And don’t worry if you haven’t watched the new anime yet — no “Edgerunners 2” spoilers ahead!

One of the things we love about Night City is that there’s always another story unfolding somewhere. V may be central to the events of Cyberpunk 2077 , but they’re hardly the only merc in town, fighting to survive and make a name for themselves on those neon-soaked streets. Every fixer has clients, every crew has gigs to take care of, every Night City merc has their story — and sometimes, those stories collide in unexpected ways.

That’s exactly what happens in the brand-new quest introduced with the “Edgerunners 2” Update. What begins as just another gig from Wakako turns into an action-packed, high-stakes mission that sees V cross paths with Weak Kingsley, a famed Night City merc and one of the main characters of “Edgerunners 2.” We won’t spoil what happens, but during the course of this mission, V has a chance to assist Weak and his crew during a risky gig that takes place in a brand-new location: Night City Prison.

The new “Edgerunners 2” gig is more than a chance to encounter characters from the anime in the game — it serves as a prequel to the events of the series. So, play the quest before watching the anime, and you’ll have a little extra context going into Episode 1. Already seen the show? Then with this gig, you’ll get to revisit part of Weak’s story with a broader perspective of him and his crew.

And there’s even more forEdgerunnersfans in this update. For starters, you can find and equip Weak’s full outfit — vest, glasses, coat, pants, the works — and get your hands on his signature revolver, Coronation. We’ve also added a new radio station, HKGN 102.FM, featuring official tracks from both “Cyberpunk: Edgerunners” and “Edgerunners 2.” So if you’re planning to spend a few more hours cruising around Night City after watching the show, we’ve got your soundtrack covered.

What’s better than blasting your way through a warehouse full of gangoons with a revolver, dealing one headshot after another? Doing it with two revolvers, obviously.

That’s right — dual wielding is here! With the Edgerunners 2 Update, you can raise hell with a pistol or revolver in each hand. That’s a whole new vibe — and a whole new level of awesome.

But dual wielding isn’t just about looking cool. It brings a new playstyle and a fresh way to approach combat — in fact, it’s one of the most significant gameplay additions to the game’s combat since Update 2.0 introduced throwing knives. So if you’ve been looking for an excuse to shake up your fighting style, this might just be it.

Cyberware enhances your stats and abilities — but what if it could take your style to the next level, too? That’s where glamdocs come in. These new vendors let you customize the appearance of your cyberware, with 40 styles in different colors to choose from. Fancy a new look for your chrome? Pay them a visit at one (or all) of the five locations across Night City and see what catches your eye.

In a city that lives and dies by appearances, V really can’t afford to pass up any opportunity to shake up their look. On top of cyberware customization, we’ve also added 20 new hairstyles and several clothing sets to give your V the best chance of standing out, even in Night City.

We know how creative the Cyberpunk 2077 community can be, and we’re always curious to see what players come up with. That’s why we’re introducing cross-platform mod support through mod.io integration.

The update adds a Mods panel where you can browse and install supported community-created content directly in the game. It’s a new way to experiment with your experience, and we’re looking forward to seeing how it develops as more mods become available and receive support over time!

We’ve covered some of the bigger additions, but there’s still plenty to find in the Edgerunners 2 Update.

items.title: Cyberpunk 2 lead confirms “half of the quest team” are modders as CDPR strives to continue supporting the next generation of modding
items.summary: CD Projekt Red confirms that the Cyberpunk 2 quest team largely consists of modders as they push to support the next generation of modding.
items.content:
Games Blog About Us Careers Tutorials FAQs All News Features Guides Reviews Fortnite Marvel Rivals Arc Raiders Tutorials FAQs Cyberpunk 2 lead confirms “half of the quest team” are modders as CDPR strives to continue supporting the next generation of modding Published:

CD Projekt Red’s Cyberpunk 2 is years away from release, but fans are still eagerly awaiting the upcoming sequel. As it turns out, a significant number of fans are also actively working on the game with half of the game’s quest team consisting of modders.

Right now, Cyberpunk 2 is still in pre-production with the game’s concepts continually evolving within CDPR’s new Boston studio. While the game appears to be taking the same first-person-only stance as the original , we have no idea what the game’s narrative hook will be.

With that said, Cyberpunk 2 associate game director and former quest design lead on Cyberpunk 2077 confirmed in a recent livestream that much of the new game’s quest team consists of modders from previous CDPR games.

Sasko explained that modding is still “a foot-in-the-door technique, and a gateway into game dev”. While Cyberpunk 2 is moving from RedEngine to Unreal Engine 5 , modders showed how to make content that fits the world and vibe of the RPG franchise, which was invaluable to CDPR’s new studio.

“You can see and you can learn how things are made—how things can be built,” Sasko continued. “We actually hired so many modders [for Cyberpunk 2]. I would say, at this point, half of the quest team is all former modders.”

Sasko explained that these modders aren’t just from Cyberpunk 2077, but prior games as well. “They were are modders before of The Witcher 3, Witcher 2, you know, before we hired them and they’re part of our company, and it’s a wonderful way to actually start your career and really learn and see how to actually built those things.”

For CDPR, this is why modding is so important with the studio hoping to continue supporting modders into the future. If their games support modding and help create new generations of modders, then they’ve in turn created the next generation of CDPR developers as well.

“That’s just another thing that really excited me,” he said. “That we can keep kind of pushing this thing and make it more available for more players.”

The Witcher and Cyberpunk games are not games that require mods to be enjoyed, but modders have created some truly spectacular experiences for both. (I’m proud to announce myself as a strong lover of The Witcher 3 cloaks mods which give Geralt unparalleled pizzaz).

With that said, mods bring additional longevity to pretty much every game that supports modding, and Cyberpunk specifically has hugely benefitted from the work of modders. From new missions to perks and skill tree reworks, it’s understandable why many only play CDPR’s iconic RPG with mods enabled, and hiring those incredible creators is a great step towards creating an unforgettable sequel.

Lewis White is a veteran games journalist with over a decade in the field. Starting with beloved Xbox website ICXM/XboxMAD, Lewis became the Gaming Editor at MSPoweruser before becoming the Editor in Chief of StealthOptional and Gfinityesports. Lewis later jumped to By Gamers For Gamers where he jumped to become EIC of VideoGamer and the host of the New VideoGamer Podcast prior to the website’s acquisition.

Over the years, Lewis has also seen long-form investigative pieces published in outlets such as Eurogamer, PCGamesN, Wireframe, Retro Gamer, Nintendo Life, and EDGE. Now, as the Editor in Chief of FRVR Blog, Lewis strives to bring the same level of quality journalism with interview-led content to the site in both written and audio form with the FRVR Podcast.

With a First Degree BA Hons in Games Journalism and Public Relations, Lewis has been a stable part of the British games press for over a decade, and has frequently displayed his love of Halo, The Elder Scrolls, Fallout, and other games pretty much everywhere he’s worked. And FRVR is no different.

And if you want to know even more, read through the list of most important changes below:

Edgerunners Content

Technology

Fixes

items.content:
To survive in Night City, you need someone to watch your back. On the way to the major leagues, V managed to gather a remarkable crew. You could even say, a crew to remember!

From trusted allies to unforgettable personalities, these are the people who helped shape V’s journey through the City of Dreams. This episode of It’s All About You is dedicated to the legendary crew that stood by V through every high and low.

Thank you for staying with us and expressing your love for Cyberpunk 2077 in the most creative ways possible. Don’t forget to check out our gallery to see more works, and, of course, share your creations with us: http://cdpred.ly/AAY

See you in the next episode!

items.content:
Listen up, Samurai! 🤘🔥

Celebrate five years of Cyberpunk 2077 in this special anniversary episode of It’s All About You, looking back on Night City’s unforgettable stories through the legends and music you met along your journey!

Sure, the city’s full of noise — sirens, synths, gunfire in the distance — but if there’s one song that became its soul, it’s “Never Fade Away.”

We brought together legendary artists from across the city of dreams to reinterpret this iconic track — each in their own voice, their own style, their own rebellion. ❤️‍🔥

Plug in, turn it up, and dive into our latest It’s All About You episode.

Because legends don’t fade.

items.content:
Patch 2.31 for Cyberpunk 2077 is now live!

This update includes an AutoDrive upgrade and Photo Mode adjustments. It also addresses common issues encountered by players. For details, check the full list of changes below:

Vehicles

  • Updated AutoDrive. When driving to a selected point, the vehicle now drives smoothly, overtakes blocking vehicles and no longer stops at traffic lights. Free Roam mode has also been upgraded to follow traffic rules and navigate the city more reliably.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Johnny always spawned in the passenger seat when using the Delamain Cab service.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where applying CrystalCoat to the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru caused its wheels to flash in different colors.

    [/*]

Photo Mode

  • Most of the new poses introduced in Update 2.3 now work with any gender.

    [/*]

  • Disabled NPC collision, which will make it easier to position NPCs on top of other objects with collision (e.g. on car hoods).

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where some of the poses didn't work for Royce.

    [/*]

Quests & Open World

  • Freedom - Fixed the journal entry that appears when the player chooses not to steal the Rayfield Caliburn "Mordred."

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where, after V fails to pursue and stop Semimaru and receives a text from River saying he'll contact V soon, the follow-up message never arrives.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Fixed an issue where the Yaiba Semimaru could flip over during the chase, preventing the player from entering it.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - It's no longer possible to trigger the quest if River died during The Hunt.

    [/*]

  • Motorbreath - Players can now acquire the Yaiba ARV-Q340 Semimaru through AUTOFIXER even if they failed The Hunt, which normally unlocks the side quest where the vehicle is obtained.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed a game crash that could occur in certain circumstances after leaving the Yaiba showroom event.

    [/*]

  • Nitro (Youth Energy) - Fixed an issue where the proxy interface UI in the Yaiba showroom is cut off when the "Larger HUD Elements" setting is enabled.

    [/*]

Miscellaneous

  • Fixed several localization and lipsync issues in various languages.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle to disable vignette. It can be found in Settings → Graphics → Basic.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on PC and Mac where Ray-Traced Reflections might not display correctly when enabled under certain conditions.

    [/*]

  • Fixed several issues with displaying text messages from Delamain.

    [/*]

  • Various fixes for fluff vendors.

    [/*]

PC-specific

  • Fixed an issue where NVIDIA Reflex could be disabled while DLSS Frame Generation was enabled, causing the screen to turn pink.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Path Tracing didn't activate properly in certain scenarios.

    [/*]

Mac-specific

  • Fixed an issue where changing graphics presets on Mac set Screen Space Reflections to a higher setting compared to the equivalent presets on PC.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue causing a permanent white screen when Frame Generation is enabled while entering the braindance in The Information.

    [/*]

  • Selecting "Defaults" in Video Settings no longer turns HDR Mode off.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where setting the MetalFX DRS Maximum Resolution above the value applied by the “For this Mac” preset could cause visual artifacts.

    [/*]

  • Fixed the inverted behavior of the "Mute Game in Background" toggle in Settings.

    [/*]

  • Removed the outdated "(Requires Game Restart)" disclaimer from the mouseover description of the "Disable Spatial Audio" setting.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue on the App Store version that caused the game to become stuck on the “Press Space to continue” breaching screen.

    [/*]

  • Various stability and performance optimizations.

    [/*]
